#6259. These 9 Hotels for Broadway Lovers Put You in the Heart of NYC’s Theater District

As a Californian who discovered the wonderful world of Broadway by borrowing CDs from my local library, it was only fitting that the first trip I ever planned by myself was to New York City—and the entire itinerary revolved around collecting Playbills. Now, after living in the area for more than two decades, I’m that unlikely New Yorker who still claims Times Square as her favorite and most-frequented neighborhood. I just love the Theater District—where else can you find 41 venues featuring the world's best live theater all within a single mile?

In this age of event tourism, Broadway has remained a constant. And seeing a show is about more than just the storyline of a play or the numbers in a musical—it’s an experience that you’re a part of. Over my 20 years as an entertainment editor and journalist, I’ve interviewed numerous Broadway stars, and they always say they feed off of, and are fueled by, audience reactions. You’re not just a passive viewer; your presence drives the show. It's something special to take part in.

If you've got a Broadway trip in your future, chances are you're going to need a hotel that will help you maximize your experience. The list below features properties with themed suites, theater lore, and locations just steps from the Great White Way. Read on for the best places to stay in NYC for a show-stopping Broadway getaway.

Closest theaters: 1-minute walk to Palace Theatre, 3-minute walk to James Earl Jones Theatre and Lunt-Fontanne TheatreWhy we love it: Right across from Palace Theatre, pre- and post-show prix-fixe menus, Studio 54 history

These days, Studio 54 is one of Broadway’s most popular stages (currently home to The Rocky Horror Show ), but back in 1977, Ian Schrager opened it as a nightclub, and it has since come to epitomize celebrity culture for a generation. Schrager brought that same visionary spirit when he opened the 452-room Times Square Edition in 2019, just across the street from the Palace Theatre. One of my favorite spots in Times Square is the hotel's Terrace and Outdoor Garden, a lush dining oasis that offers three-course Broadway Express prix-fixe menus both pre- and post-show. For those looking for an upgraded theater experience, the Edition's Showstopping Stay package—which can be booked up to 10 days in advance—includes two premium tickets to select shows, dinner with Champagne, theater-themed amenities, and house-made snacks.

Closest theaters: 9-minute walk to Studio 54, 10-minute walk to Vivian Beaumont Theater, 11-minute walk to Broadway TheatreWhy we love it: Central Park views, Broadway VIP Experience

Though a few blocks north of the Theater District thrills, the Mandarin Oriental is still less than a 15-minute walk to most theaters—yet it feels a world apart. It overlooks Central Park in one direction, and its 75-foot lap pool has views of the Hudson River. Guests are pampered with a true five-star experience every step of the way, whether it’s raising a glass at The Bar speakeasy or lounging around at celeb-favorite MO Lounge. You can also rub shoulders with the stars via the hotel's Broadway VIP Experience package, which includes an hour-long meet-and-greet with a Broadway cast member over bites and Champagne at the lounge. Also included are orchestra tickets (choose from 13 shows, including Hamilton and Harry Potter and the Cursed Child) and show merch, as well as add-ons like a theater transfer in a Mercedes, a 90-minute guided tour of the Museum of Broadway, or even acting lessons or a private concert with a stage star.

Closest theaters: 3-minute walk to Belasco Theatre, 4-minute walk to Hudson Theatre, 5-minute walk to Stephen Sondheim TheatreWhy we love it: Official partner of the Tony Awards, recently refreshed, early check-in option

If hotels could earn Tonys, the Sofitel New York would be a clear winner. As a longtime partner of Broadway’s iconic awards show, many a theater star has walked through its doors. That includes George Clooney during his Broadway debut in Good Night, and Good Luck, Jonathan Groff during his turn as Bobby Darin in Just in Time, and Mia Farrow while she was in The Roommate. Just last year, the property underwent a full makeover, reimagining its 398 rooms and suites (some with Empire State Building views), as well as its lobby, fitness center, and dining options (including Social 45 Bar & Bistro), drawing on the Art Deco glamour of Paris and New York. While an exclusive Broadway package is currently in the works, the Sofitel does currently offer The Ultimate Manhattan Luxury Staycation experience, which includes a welcome drink, dining credit, signature pastries, and early check-in at noon, perfect for squeezing in an extra Wednesday or weekend matinee.

Closest theaters: 2-minute walk to Eugene O’Neill Theatre, Walter Kerr, and Longacre TheatreWhy we love it: Quiet, designed by a Tony-winning scenic designer, curated theater mementos

Despite being footsteps away from several Broadway theaters, Civilian Hotel manages to create a cozy boutique experience, starting with an entrance just around the corner from Eighth Avenue. One step inside, and you feel like you’ve earned a backstage pass— hotelier Jason Pomeranc teamed up with scenic designer David Rockwell (Hairspray, Legally Blonde, Elf) on a classic theater theme featuring everything from marquee-inspired lighting to dramatic curtains. Even its 203 guest rooms channel vintage dressing room vibes. Rockwell's goal was to create a space for NYC’s creatives—performers, designers, directors, producers, and writers—that paid homage to classic Broadway. Stop by the Blue Vault tasting room and lounge to spot some theater relics, and the Olio Collection rooftop bar for more than 250 pieces of theater-inspired art.

Closest theaters: 1-minute walk to Palace Theatre, 3-minute walk to Marquis TheatreWhy we love it: Location across from TKTS booth, buzzy Sky Lobby

When it comes to Theater District locations, you can't find much better than the 661-room Tempo by Hilton New York Times Square. Making its debut in the dense area in August 2023, it snagged a prime spot right across from Duffy Square’s TKTS booth, the bright red discount ticket outlet that sells last-minute show tickets for up to 50% off (psst, check here for today’s offers). Even closer is the Palace Theatre, currently home to the musical The Lost Boys, which the property has partnered with on a themed suite, bookable through September 14, 2027. Inside the suite, you'll find an ’80s seaside feel mimicking the musical’s world of Santa Carla.

Closest theaters: 2-minute walk to Eugene O’Neill Theatre, Walter Kerr, and Ambassador Theatre; half a dozen more a 3-minute walk awayWhy we love it: Vacation vibes at its Bar Sprezzatura, daily complimentary wine in the Living Room Lobby during Evening Social Hour, Roundabout Theatre Company partnership

The first time I stepped off the elevator into Kimpton Theta New York’s Bar Sprezzatura, I immediately craved an Aperol spritz. That’s how much I was transported to the Italian Riviera. The contrast between the lively Midtown streets below (the bar sits on the 15th floor) and the laid-back rooftop bar made me fall in love with the 364-key property instantly, and with multiple two- and three-bedroom suites, it's perfect for families and groups looking to book a foodie-friendly Broadway bonding trip. This November, the hotel launched the Roundabout Theatre Co. x Kimpton Theta package, giving guests 20% off tickets to Roundabout Theatre Co. shows (currently The Rocky Horror Show and Imaginary Invalid) plus pre- or post-show drinks at the bar.

Closest theaters: Attached to Marquis Theatre, 1-minute walk to Minskoff Theatre, 2-minute walk to Richard Rodgers TheatreWhy we love it: Ideal for Marquis Theatre shows, home to NYC’s only rotating restaurant, Broadway Bound Dining Package

For a mega-sized hotel smack dab in the middle of Times Square, the Marriott Marquis still has a sense of character. When I first moved to the area 23 years ago, I used to frequent its eight-floor Broadway Lounge, looking out at Times Square and marveling that I had finally “made it." Nowadays, I still pop in for a dose of nostalgia, gazing up at the 36-floor atrium’s elevators leading to the hotel's 1,900 rooms—a constant in a world that’s changed so much since it opened in 1985. But that throwback feel comes with a new spring in its step, most notably at its 48th-floor spinning restaurant, The View, reimagined by Danny Meyer in 2024. (Note: TodayTix members get free bubbly and bar snacks here, depending on their tier.) But what makes the property so unique for theater fans is that it’s the only hotel ever built with a Broadway theater inside—yes, the Marquis Theatre is literally on the third floor. Also special: The Broadway Bound Dining Package includes the chance to mingle with a theater star!

Closest theaters: 2-minute walk to the Nederlander Theatre, New Amsterdam Theatre, and Lyric TheatreWhy we love it: Themed rooms, located on 42nd Street, close to other attractions

Now here’s a hotel that reflects both “A Whole New World” and “The Circle of Life.” Through its partnership with Disney’s two long-running musicals, Hilton New York Times Square guests can go all in with themed rooms curated by Broadway designer Devin Sparkles Design. Aladdin's Times Square Palace Suite is decked out just like Agrabah, down to a genie lamp, Moroccan magic carpets, and Jasmine-inspired silks. Over in The Lion King’s Royal Suite, it’s all about the wonders of the Serengeti Pridelands, with hand-painted Rafiki-like patterns and bird puppets flying from the ceiling. Both include wake-up calls from each musical’s most iconic characters—the Genie and Rafiki—as well as themed drinks. But perhaps the most valuable part of the package, especially for those driving in? Parking in Times Square.

Closest theaters: 1-minute walk to Hudson Theatre, Belasco Theatre, and Lyceum Theatre

Why we love it: Passageway running between Hudson Theatre’s entrance and stage door, June 2026 refresh

Ever since my first Broadway trip to NYC in 2002, I’ve been stage-dooring shows. The Hudson Theatre shows can be tricky for this, as the theater’s entrance is on 44th Street, but its stage door is on 45th. It wasn’t until I discovered that the Millennium Hotel had a secret passageway—which is also the entrance to the hotel—that I started snagging spots close enough to get autographs (including from Daniel Radcliffe during Merrily We Roll Along). That said, I've always been jealous of those actually staying at the 751-room property, with a trio of theaters literally at their doorstep. Those eager to dive even deeper into the Theater District's history will love that the property is just across the street from the Museum of Broadway.

Is it expensive to see a show on Broadway?

Yes, price tags can be high—the year-to-date average per ticket for 2026 is $122.67. But there are also plenty of ways to find discounts through lotteries, TodayTix, Theatr, and the TKTS Booth. I’ve only paid more than $100 five times in my life—and never more than $200. (That’s why I haven’t been to a movie in nearly a decade, but have seen nearly 40 shows in the last year!)

What show should I see on Broadway this winter?

For last-minute trips, hot tickets right now include Bowen Yang’s record-breaking run in Cole Escola’s Oh, Mary! (Lyceum Theatre), plus A Few Good Men (Vivian Beaumont Theatre), Much Ado About Nothing (Winter Garden), Other Desert Cities (Hudson Theatre), and School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play (Samuel J. Friedman). And of course there are long-running hits like Wicked (Gershwin Theatre), Hamilton (Richard Rodgers Theatre), Harry Potter and the Cursed Child (Lyric Theatre), The Great Gatsby (Broadway Theatre), and Disney’s The Lion King (Minskoff Theatre).

Are there any shows I should plan a 2027 trip around?

As we’re standing on the precipice of one of the most anticipated Broadway seasons, there’s no better time to plan a theater getaway. Coming soon are Dolly: A True Original Musical (opening December 7 at St. James Theatre), the Julia Roberts and Paul Rudd–led Small Mouth Sounds (February 10 at Ethel Barrymore Theatre), Jonathan Groff’s The Amish Project (February 10 at Broadhurst Theatre), Dirty Dancing (February 12 at Lena Thorne Theatre), Evita on Broadway (February 27 at Winter Garden Theatre), Lin-Manuel Miranda’s Warriors (March 9 at Lunt-Fontanne Theatre), Purple Rain (March 12 at Majestic Theatre), The Sound of Music (March 23 at Vivian Beaumont Theatre), Damn Yankees (March 24 at Marquis Theatre), and the one I’m most thrilled about, the West End transfer Paddington: The Musical (March 30 at Al Hirschfield Theatre)—I already have my ticket for the first preview!

Every hotel review on this list has been written by a Condé Nast Traveler journalist who knows the destination and has visited that property. When choosing hotels, our editors consider properties across price points that offer an authentic and insider experience of a destination, keeping design, location, service, and sustainability credentials top of mind.

As the most discerning, up-to-the-minute voice in all things travel, Condé Nast Traveler is the global citizen’s bible and muse, offering both inspiration and vital intel. We understand that time is the greatest luxury, which is why Condé Nast Traveler mines its network of experts and influencers so that you never waste a meal, a drink, or a hotel stay wherever you are in the world.

#6258. A Wonderfully Relaxing “Afternoon Matinée” In SAS A330 Business Class

Our SAS A330-300 Business Class flight from Copenhagen to Chicago could not have been better and it really was one of the most relaxing flights I’ve had in a long time, during which I enjoyed great food and watched two excellent movies when I could not sleep.

Unless I’m flying on a plane with Starlink, I assume that the internet is not going to work onboard (especially on SAS). If it does, it is a pleasant surprise. If not, in most cases I will have already completed essential tasks so that I’m not spending my flight dreading unfinished work.

We flew home on Sunday afternoon, also a day off for me, and I decided that I’d just relax and watch some movies during the flight if I could not sleep between meals.

Lunch, by the way, was delicious. I pre-ordered “ASC” salmon with tomato vinaigrette, summer cabbage with brown butter, Jerusalem artichoke soufflé, and chive oil while Heidi pre-ordered beef with osso buco sauce, polenta cake, butter-and-thyme carrot, grilled artichoke and gremolata. We shared. Both dishes were perfect.

The appetizer and dessert were also excellent, as was the coffee:

I find the catering consistently excellent on SAS.

I did try to sleep, but could not, but that turned out to be a blessing in disguise on this flight. First I watched a Japanese movie called A Pale View of Hills, which I found riveting and very well-done. It trace the story of Etsuko and has a beautiful twist that left me profoundly moved. Highly recommended.

Meanwhile, Heidi was watching a German movie called Sound of Falling, a psychological drama spanning a century at a farmhouse in rural Germany. I then watched that while she watched the Japanese move. Wow, also excellent. Riveting and thought-provoking.

We don’t have a TV at home and I do not watch movies or anything at all unless I’m on a plane, but watching movies like this makes me think that I may be missing out…both were so well done and absolutely worth the time. I honestly could not stop thinking about either one for a couple days.

Before a landing, a delicious open-face sandwich was served with eggs and shrimp.

The flight crew was excellent and the kids were again very well-behaved, so I really don’t think it could have been a better flight. SAS does not have a cutting edge business class seat, but between my six hours of sleep on the way to Copenhagen and my restful flight on the way back, I was reminded again how much I love fly SAS Business Class and hope that I can find a way to replenish my EuroBonus account once we spend down the rest of the two million points.

I’m not sure whether I will offer a full review of this flight…I took a lot more pictures, but I’ve reviewed this product recently and little has changed. Bottom line: I do strongly recommend SAS for intercontinental travel.

#6257. 15 Best Grand Canyon Hotels, Rentals, and Glampsites for Sleeping in Style Under the Stars

A mile deep and 277 miles long, the Grand Canyon is a jaw-droppingly majestic chasm in Arizona’s rust-red desert that’s speckled with pinyon pines. Standing on its edge, one can’t help but feel small, watching the mighty Colorado River churn vigorously along the ravine’s bottom. Whether you’re hoping for a challenging all-day hike to the canyon’s floor, a soul-stirring overlook near the visitor center, or a multi-day rafting expedition, this national park has all that (and more) in spades. It’s hardly a surprise that it drew more than 4.4 million visitors in 2025 alone, so you know you'll have some competition when it comes to finding the best place to stay nearby.

Personally, I like to stay as close as possible to the park, to make the most of dreamy desert sunrises and maximize my time on the trails. Grand Canyon is famous for its historic lodges and quirky Route 66 nostalgia, which can make picking the perfect spot for your crew a little overwhelming. Cozy cabin or fancy, family-sized rental? Canvas glamping tent under the stars or a fun getaway that’s in the heart of the action? I’ve sorted through the hundreds of options so you don’t have to. Here are my favorite Grand Canyon hotels, glamping sites, vacation rentals, and cabins for a memorable stay in and around this utterly striking national park.

Number of guests: 8Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Full kitchen, colorful decor, telescope

Location: Valle, ArizonaThings to do nearby: Kaibab National Forest, Grand Canyon Village, Rim Trail

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 1 bathWhy we love it: Telescope, soaking tub, firepit, secluded location

This fantastic two-bedroom wilderness retreat is situated on two private acres filled with fragrant juniper trees in the arid Arizona desert. Though it’s full of modern creature comforts (like high-speed Wi-Fi, a smart TV, two plush queen beds, and stainless steel kitchen appliances), this guesthouse is also fit for nature lovers, with amenities like an outdoor firepit, comfy front porch, and even a telescope for late-night stargazing. The home also boasts a coveted location that’s right between the city of Williams and the South Rim entrance gates near Tusayan.

Location: Williams, ArizonaThings to do nearby: Grand Canyon Railroad, Pete's Route 66 Gas Station Museum

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: Studio, 1 bathWhy we love it: Open kitchen, fenced backyard, washer and dryer

Prepare to enjoy lofted ceilings and an airy, open floor plan at this home in Flagstaff. When the weather’s nice, light up the gas-powered grill, sit by the firepit, and enjoy alfresco dining in the property’s fully fenced backyard. Inside, guests can unwind with a 65-inch flat-screen TV, a king and queen bed (on the main floor and in the loft, respectively), a full kitchen, and split air-conditioning that keeps the space comfortable no matter the season. Best of all, the house is located smack dab in the heart of the city, near funky bars and fabulous restaurants.

Location: Flagstaff, ArizonaThings to do nearby: Foxglenn Park, Elden Pueblo Heritage Site, Picture Canyon Natural and Cultural Preserve

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 1 bathTop amenities: Outdoor patio, desert vistas, eat-in kitchen

Bright whites, natural light, and pops of blue bring fun character to this modern desert casita, situated right off Route 66 in Williams. At 529 square feet, this cute, pet-friendly cabin epitomizes indoor-outdoor living, with 12 private acres of serene desert surrounding it, plus a gorgeous patio for post-park cocktails with friends. Enjoy fast Wi-Fi, smart TVs, and a Keurig coffee maker, all while sleeping just 20 minutes from the park’s South Rim.

Location: Williams, ArizonaThings to do nearby: Kaibab National Forest, Grand Canyon Village

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Skylight, solar power, desert views

Calling all adventurous couples: this light-soaked tiny home is a dreamy, romantic escape. A mere 30-minute drive from the Grand Canyon, this off-grid spot is the perfect place to sip a glass of wine and stare at the stars after a day of hiking through craggy red rocks. Take in the sunrise from the enclosed outdoor shower, or sip coffee in the airy kitchen. After dark, snuggle up by the firepit and test your astronomy knowledge while you point out constellations from the outdoor seating area. With so much open space, you’ll feel like you’re a million miles from anywhere.

Location: Valle, ArizonaThings to do nearby: Mather Point, Yavapai Geology Museum

Boasting three bedrooms with plush bedding (the rooms have a king, a queen, and two trundles, respectively) and two bathrooms, this off-grid, solar-powered cabin is the perfect home base for your entire crew after a day exploring the Grand Canyon’s South Rim. Situated 30 minutes from the park’s entrance station, this home offers sweeping views of the San Francisco Peaks, a full kitchen with gas appliances, and an indoor fireplace—all set on an ultra-secluded piece of land in the desert.

Over the last few years, Under Canvas has earned itself a sparkling reputation as a top purveyor of luxurious glamping experiences. From organic bath products and morning yoga to nightly s’mores around the fire, it has comfortable camping dialed in—so much so that even the choosiest hotel snob will feel right at home. Pro tip: Splurge on a stargazer tent for dreamy Milky Way views without ever leaving your bed.

Location: Valle, ArizonaThings to do nearby: Grand Canyon IMAX, Mather Point

Number of guests: VariesBed and bath: VariesWhy we love it: On-site dining, desert-themed decor, Navajo canyon guides

Perched at the edge of the Vermillion Cliffs about five miles from Lees Ferry (the launch point for multi-day rafting trips on the Colorado River), Marble Canyon Lodge is a new base camp for travelers looking to explore this less-touristed side of the Grand Canyon. Here, adventure seekers have their pick of colorful, refreshed motel digs, from two-bedroom cottages to no-frills king bedrooms with tea kettles and gear storage areas. Start your morning on the porch with a cup of Lucky Foot coffee as the canyon walls turn amber with the first light, then fuel up at the Lonely Jackrabbit Restaurant, the only real eatery for many miles, which serves up Southwestern fare, like cactus burritos and epic burgers, seven days a week.

This dreamy Aman property is one of a kind. Set in remote Canyon Point, Utah, Amangiri is a rare breed of luxury hotel because it truly blends in with the natural landscape that surrounds it. From canvas-lined pavilions with private plunge pools to a four-bedroom mesa home, guests here get to mingle with high sandstone bluffs and rose-hued cliffs, no matter which room they pick. Plus, with an on-site via ferrata and in-house guides at the ready to help book national park outings, experiencing the best of canyon country is a cinch. (Of note, this is the farthest hotel from the Grand Canyon on my list, at two and a half hours away.)

Why not pair a luxe spa vacation with your Grand Canyon adventure? L’Auberge de Sedona offers elegant creekside cottages and lodge rooms with verdant garden views, ideal for the discerning traveler who likes their hikes with a side of Swedish massage. Open year-round in the high-desert mecca of Sedona, two hours from the park, the lodge boasts a bevy of daily activities (think Qigong meditation and chakra-balancing yoga) as well as a mindful fine-dining menu at Cress on Oak Creek, the on-site restaurant.

Location: SedonaThings to do nearby: Cathedral Rock, Devil’s Bridge Trail, Slide Rock State Park

Number of guests: VariesBed and bath: VariesWhy we love it: Magical views, private decks, world-class wellness at Mii Amo

Soak up the magic of red rock country by immersing yourself in the hip, Southwestern flair of Sedona. Enchantment Resort is set in the heart of the Vermillion Bluffs of Boynton Canyon, with adorable casitas and roomy suites for groups of up to 10. This pet-friendly hotel oozes with thoughtful architectural details, like log ceiling beams, gas fireplaces, and sienna-tinted adobe clay, with elevated American cuisine at its restaurant, Che Ah Chi.

Location: SedonaThings to do nearby: Boynton Canyon hikes and mountain biking, Seven Sacred Pools

When is the best time to visit Grand Canyon National Park?

With an elevation spanning 2,000 feet to 8,000 feet, Grand Canyon experiences a wide range of temperatures on any given day. Thus, the best season to visit greatly depends on what your adventure priorities are.

If you’re planning to raft “the big ditch” with a guide, go between April and October for warm, sunny days that perfectly contrast the 50-degree Colorado River. Hoping to hike to the bottom and camp at Bright Angel? Don your favorite traction devices atop the canyon to crunch through seasonal ice and book a backcountry permit for late fall, winter, or early spring. Auto tourists who want to explore the canyon’s south rim by car can travel in virtually any season—just be prepared for crowds in summer months and occasional snow closures at the height of winter.

Lastly, a good rule of thumb for intrepid travelers hiking down into the canyon is that you’ll gain roughly 5 degrees for every 1,000 feet you descend. Plan on it being 20 degrees warmer at the bottom of the canyon than it is at the rim. The National Park Service (NPS) does not recommend hiking to the bottom of the canyon during summer months, as temperatures at Phantom Ranch often surpass 100 degrees.

How do you get to Grand Canyon National Park?

If you’re planning to fly in, the closest major airports are Sky Harbor International in Phoenix and Harry Reid International in Las Vegas, but both are at least a three-hour drive away, so you’ll want to rent a car and crank up the tunes to brave the journey. Regional airports are scattered around the area, most notably in small-but-commercial Flagstaff, Sedona, and Tusayan. There’s also a vintage train service that runs daily from Williams, Arizona.

Notably, Grand Canyon National Park is a stone’s throw away from one of the most iconic road trips the US has to offer–historic Route 66. Running from Chicago all the way to the Pacific Coast in Santa Monica, California, this legendary trip ventures across northern Arizona on Interstate 40.

What are the best things to do in Grand Canyon National Park?

Spanning 23 breathtaking miles between Grand Canyon Village and the Desert View area, Desert View Drive is the only scenic byway in the park that’s open year-round to private vehicles. Enjoy Mary Colter’s iconic Desert View Watchtower, which was inspired by ancestral Puebloan architecture and features murals by Hopi artist Fred Kabotie, at the park’s far eastern edge.

Another popular drive along the South Rim is the winding Hermit Road, which ends at the historic stone structure of Hermit’s Rest that date back to 1914. The drive is only open to private vehicles in December, January, and February; in all other months, travelers must use the park’s free shuttle system, hopping on and off at popular sites.

Though the hiking distance between the canyon’s north and south rims is a scant 21 miles, the drive to get between the two is a circuitous 220 miles. As a result, only 10% of the national park’s visitors set foot on the just-as-striking North Rim. This high-elevation outpost (over 8,000 feet) and log cabin-style lodge have a shorter visitation season than the South Rim (you’ll have to travel there between May 15 and October 15 most years), but adventurous drivers desperate to escape the crowds should make a beeline for the pinyon and ponderosa pine–studded views of crumbling crimson sandstone along Cape Royal Road. Plus, you’ll be within easy driving distance of Zion, if you’d like to extend your journey.

If you’re into hiking past dramatic vermillion outcroppings, secret waterfalls, and hanging gardens, you’re in the right place. The Grand Canyon also boasts some of the most stunning wheelchair-accessible paths in the country (check out the 13-mile, mostly-paved Rim Trail), as well as hamstring-busting overnight treks into the belly of the ravine.

For an epic out-and-back excursion with much of the expansive red rock scenery you’d find on a longer jaunt, head to South Kaibab Trailhead and venture just under a mile downhill to the aptly named Ooh Aah Point. Want a little more bang for your buck? Continue down to Skeleton Point for a sweeping panorama of the Colorado River (six miles round trip). Bright Angel Trailhead is another iconic starting point for a day hike or overnight trek into the canyon. Lace up your boots for a three-mile round-trip stroll to the shade structure at Mile-and-a-Half Resthouse or, if you’re an experienced hiker looking to sweat, start early for an all-day 12-mile journey to jaw-dropping views of Plateau Point.

Trekking to the bottom of the Grand Canyon and back is the stuff hiking bucket lists are made of. But due to midday heat and the extremely strenuous nature of these hikes, the National Park Service does not recommend aiming to complete such a journey in a single day. It’s highly recommended to nab a backcountry permit and camp overnight at one of the many below-the-rim sites (like Bright Angel Campground or Havasupai Gardens). Pro tip: Use the free park shuttle and create a loop starting at South Kaibab and ending at the Bright Angel Trailhead. Heading for the quieter North Rim? Tramp down the North Kaibab Trail for two miles (one-way) to Supai Tunnel.

Find our full list of the best Grand Canyon hikes here.

It’s rare that a national park offers a designated bike path along its most iconic sights, but at the Grand Canyon, visitors can spin for roughly 13 miles along the park’s dreamy South Rim vistas. BYO-bike or rent one at Canyon Adventures in the village, then steer onto the paved Greenway Trail to South Kaibab. Or, utilize the free shuttle system (yes, they’ve got bike racks) and ride the bus to Monument Creek Vista, then cruise along the South Rim to Hermits Rest.

North Rim visitors hoping to escape that South Rim fervor can enjoy loads of rugged mountain biking. A 12-mile swath of the enormous, 800-mile Arizona Trail runs right through the park.

Are there guided tours at Grand Canyon National Park?

There are dozens of phenomenal guided tours available for guests who aren’t comfortable backpacking alone or want a unique type of experience. Mule rides are a storied part of the canyon’s past and how many early tourists ventured into the canyon (sometimes in full Victorian regalia). Though it might seem like a rough place for a working animal, mules are much better equipped to handle heat and steep, rocky terrain than their horse counterparts. Plus, these rides offer below-the-rim access for visitors with mobility concerns. Today, both short day trips and extended overnight ventures to Phantom Ranch on muleback are available for those looking to pay homage to a bygone era.

For a brag-worthy addition to your hiking checklist, seek out Wildland Trekking’s guided rim-to-rim backpacking journeys (or, in winter, go big and test your skills on a rim-to-rim-to-rim hike). Craving something off the beaten path? The remote, five-day Hermit Loop offers miles of fire-red sandstone plateaus.

I’d be remiss if I didn’t mention the second-to-none river rafting to be had at Grand Canyon National Park. Grand Canyon Expeditions and Western River Expeditions have been guiding for decades and both offer first-class service for intrepid travelers looking to go the distance on the mighty Colorado.

The best rewards card for your wallet is usually one that rewards you with more of what you really enjoy. For those who love to travel, that might mean earning airline miles or hotel points to help fund the next trip.

But what if what you really love is sports?

The soon-to-be-released Fanatics American Express® Card is being designed specifically around sports fandom, rewarding fans with more of what they already love — from team merch and tickets to collectibles and more.

While the card isn't yet available for applications, we know that the upcoming Fanatics American Express Card will earn rewards in the form of FanCash, Fanatics' loyalty currency.

TPG Tip: You can join the waitlist now to be among the first to get the new Fanatics American Express Card when it is released.

FanCash is simple: $1 in FanCash equals $1 toward eligible purchases across the Fanatics ecosystem, from team merch on Fanatics.com to tickets in the Fanatics App and purchases on Topps.com. In eligible states, it can also be redeemed for rewards like bonus bets in Fanatics Sportsbook & Casino.

So whether you want your team's newest jersey, a collectible from a Fanatics auction or tickets to your team's next game, you'll have plenty of ways to put your FanCash to use.

When it comes to earning FanCash, here's what the new Fanatics American Express Card will offer:

And when you use the new card in the Fanatics App, you can stack rewards to earn 8% or more on purchases in the form of FanCash. That FanCash can then go toward things like apparel, tickets, trading cards, collectibles and event experiences, such as the fan favorite Fanatics Fest.

The card will have no annual fee** and will offer new cardmembers $100 in bonus FanCash after spending $1,000 on purchases within the first 90 days.***

Cardmembers can earn another $100 in bonus FanCash after spending at least $500 per month on eligible purchases for 12 consecutive months.†

Earning rewards on your spending is great, but the Fanatics American Express Card is also designed to give cardmembers something even harder for serious sports fans to get: access.

For example, cardmembers will get early presale access to select Topps releases, which could make the difference between getting your hands on something you want and missing out entirely.§

Cardmembers will also receive elevated Fanatics ONE Member Pro status, which includes 50% off ticket fees on eligible ticket purchases in the Fanatics app.‡

And while you'll get Member Pro status simply by having the card, your card can also help you make progress toward even higher Fanatics ONE status levels — and unlock additional perks along the way.

Cardmembers will receive 2,500 tier points and earn an additional 10 tier points for every $50 in card purchases, helping them work toward higher status levels that can unlock additional perks, such as tickets to Fanatics Fest, access to special events, bonus FanCash, a Fanatics ONE concierge and more.‡

With all the perks and rewards it comes with, it shouldn’t be a shocker that the Fanatics American Express Card was going to look cool, too.

And in fact, it’s almost a collectible of sorts on its own. You'll have 500+ card art options to choose from, featuring athletes across the NBA, NFL, WWE and UFC, with a unique Topps-inspired design that lets you rep your fandom every time you pull out your card.

The new Fanatics American Express Card won't just get you access to select drops and earn FanCash. Since the card is powered by the American Express Network, cardmembers will have access to Amex Offers, Amex Experiences™ — with opportunities like ticket presales — and built-in retail protections when you use the card.

There are a lot of ways the new Fanatics American Express Card stands out, but here's a truly unusual card perk.

Fanatics cardmembers will have the chance to participate in what Fanatics calls the Championship Challenge. Correctly predict the champions of the MLB, NBA, NFL and NHL, and you could get up to $100,000 of your annual spending on the Fanatics American Express Card back when the challenge launches.

That means you can put your sports knowledge to the test and have some fun following your picks throughout the year — even if you don't manage to correctly predict all four champions.

But if you do somehow nail all four? Getting up to $100,000 of your annual card spending back would certainly qualify as one of the most exciting credit card perks we've ever seen.

There are plenty of credit cards that sports fans could use, but very few are designed specifically for sports fandom.

Fanatics set out to create what it calls the “ultimate card for sports fans,” and they have certainly packed in a lot aimed squarely at that large audience.

Between early presale access to Topps releases, the ability to earn FanCash on everyday purchases and a path toward higher levels of Fanatics ONE status — not to mention the fun upcoming Championship Challenge — there are some genuinely unique perks packed into this no-annual-fee card.

#6254. Alaska, Hawaiian Pilot MECs Approve Tentative Joint Contract

Pilots at Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines are one step closer to a deal that will bring both work groups together under a single labor contract.

ALPA announced Wednesday that its Alaska and Hawaiian master executive councils unanimously approved a tentative agreement on a joint collective bargaining compact. The two councils had been negotiating since February 2025.

The proposed agreement will now go before the combined membership for a ratification vote.

Details of the agreement were not immediately available to the public.

Union officials said they worked to address the priorities of both work groups and have established a “contractual foundation for their future as a combined workforce.”

“This TA is the result of more than 600 days of challenging negotiations, countless hours of work by our volunteers, and an unwavering commitment to the pilots we represent,” Drew Coyle, the Alaska MEC chair, said in a statement. “Our Joint Negotiating Committee remained focused on the priorities of both pilot groups while working through some of the most complex issues facing our combined membership. Nothing about this process was easy. Now it’s our pilots’ turn to review the agreement, ask the tough questions, and decide whether it meets their expectations.”

Ratification voting starts Dec. 1 and closes Dec. 22.

Alaska and Hawaiian merged in 2024 and received a single operating certificate from the FAA in 2025. This effectively transformed Hawaiian from an independent airline to a brand under Alaska Air Group. Alaska has pledged to maintain Hawaiian’s brand identity, and Hawaiian retains a separate corporate leadership based in Honolulu.

The two brands have continued to integrate however, with Alaska now making use of long-haul aircraft originally owned by Hawaiian. Earlier this year, Alaska implemented a single passenger service system.

#6253. Air Canada Cancels 10 Nonstop Routes: See Full List Now

Renato Oliveira de Araujo | Shutterstock, Simple Flying

All airlines have route churn, and Air Canada is no exception. When the Star Alliance member's overall network is explored, ten routes that operated during the summer are not scheduled to return in 2027. Eight are international and two are domestic.

Air Canada is overwhelmingly the country's largest operator. OAG data for 2026 shows that it has 30% of domestic flights (WestJet is second with 21%) and 37% for the overall international arena (WestJet follows with 14%). For long-haul activity, Air Canada has 38% of the market (Air Transat is second with 11%).

They all had flights at some point between May 2026 and January 2027, but no service is scheduled thereafter. The entries include Vancouver to Singapore, which is currently the airline's longest nonstop operation. The final departure will leave British Columbia on January 24, 2027.

That link's axing was probably influenced by the high price of fuel, which worsens the economics of ultra-long-haul routes. The situation may also put a damper on any other ultra-long markets that Air Canada was considering announcing. This might have included Ho Chi Minh City, following Canada and Vietnam recently expanding their bilateral air service agreement and much speculation.

When Did Air Canada's First Flight Begin?

Montreal to New York JFK (now fully pulled out of JFK)

Toronto Pearson to New York JFK (now fully pulled out of JFK)

May 2012-April 2016. Returned in March 2023

Toronto Pearson to Charleston (now fully pulled out of Charleston)

Vancouver to Singapore (will fully pull out of Changi)

A long history of flying to Singapore, but nonstop flights started in 2024, replacing Singapore Airlines

Other eliminated routes included the thin links from Vancouver to Nashville and Raleigh-Durham, with Air Canada's flights only lasting for two seasons. It was the first time that British Columbia had nonstop service to the North Carolina airport. Nashville was different. WestJet entered the market in May 2023, providing the city pair's first-ever flights. Air Canada arrived two years later. WestJet pulled out in June 2026, followed by Canada's flag carrier three months later.

The same period was used to examine cuts to Air Canada's domestic map. Air Canada flew between Toronto Pearson and Yellowknife, in the Northwest Territories not far from the Arctic Circle, until August 2026. This year, the A319 (Rouge) and 737 MAX 8 (mainline and Rouge) were primarily used, although the A320 (mainline and Rouge) and A321 (Rouge) appeared too.

The long route, which covered 1,655 nautical miles (3,065 km) each way, launched in 2023. Flights materialized around 19 months after the debut of Air North. Perhaps unusually, Air Canada flew on a year-round basis, although winter frequencies and capacity was, of course, significantly lower than during the summer.

Following Air Canada's exit in August 2026, Air North continues to operate, primarily on the increasingly rare 737-500. Between January and October 2027, Air North's schedule submission to OAG shows that it has 37% more seats for sale than in the same period in 2026, which partly closes the capacity gap.

Only half of the seats were filled. Find out more here!

Then there is Fort McMurray, in Alberta, to which Air Canada Express stopped flying from Vancouver in May 2026. The route had been part of the carrier's network since January 2009.

First, Jazz CRJ200s operated, but flights switched to the Dash-8-Q400 in October 2015. It was pulled in June 2017 but returned in December 2025, only to last six months. The exit means that Vancouver no longer has nonstop service to Fort McMurray.

At 622 nautical miles (1,152 km), it was Air Canada's longest Q400 flight from British Columbia this year. The carrier continues to serve Fort McMurray, but from its busiest hub of Toronto Pearson, with multiple jet types and variants deployed.

#6252. SeaWorld Parks Promo Codes November 2026

Marriott Coupon CodesYou never forget your first dolphin encounter—and for many kids across the country, that often happens at SeaWorld. The beloved oceanarium puts the “amusement” in amusement parks: orcas leaping in the air, floorless rollercoasters named after sea monsters, and even aquarium sleepovers. With parks in Orlando, San Diego, San Antonio, and Abu Dhabi, SeaWorld’s aquatic allure has no bounds. SeaWorld is a top choice when it comes to taking the family out for some educational fun.

Established in 1964 by four UCLA graduates, SeaWorld began in San Diego with 22 acres, six attractions, and a handful of sea lions and dolphins (beloved orca whale Shamu arrived at the party a year later). In the early 2000s, the parks expanded with thrill rides and rollercoasters, as well as Discovery Cove, allowing visitors to interact with marine animals like bottlenose dolphins. Over the course of its history, SeaWorld has rescued over 40,000 animals and, through the SeaWorld and Busch Gardens Conservation Fund, donated over $19 million to global projects, from restoring coral reefs to preventing coastal erosion. If you want your little ones to have a whale of a time, here are the best SeaWorld Parks promo codes, discounts, and deals.

Take advantage of SeaWorld's Black Friday discounts. Save up to 60% on tickets, fun cards, and passes. Save over 50% on a single-day ticket to SeaWorld San Diego ($65 instead of $130) and enjoy increased flexibility if you visit before March 31, 2027. Combine it with the All-Day Dining option for $40, and you won't have to worry about buying meals. You can also save 40% on a 2027 Fun Card and take advantage of unlimited free visits to SeaWorld San Diego now through 2027 ($78 from $130).

SeaWorld expresses its gratitude for the service of military members through the Waves of Honor program, which grants any US active-duty military, activated or drilling reservist, or National Guardsman one complimentary admission per year, and tickets for as many as three direct dependents. Military personnel can also enjoy a 50% off discount on up to six SeaWorld Orlando single-day tickets, plus a Silver Annual Pass at SeaWorld Orlando (unlimited admission with no blockout dates for 12 months) for $161 instead of $279. Those who can take advantage of this offer will need to verify their identity via ID.Me.

For military personnel who have completed their service, SeaWorld is offering 50% off single-day tickets at SeaWorld Orlando, plus the same Silver Annual Pass discount that active-duty military members get to enjoy. To take advantage of this offer, verify with ID.Me.

If you’ve got a preschooler, give them the gift of maximum aquarium time. At SeaWorld San Antonio, kids under the age of five can enjoy free, unlimited admission to SeaWorld until January 2027, plus unlimited visits to Aquatica for only $39—just be sure to register before the offer expires on May 30. Preschool Cards are limited to Texas residents only.

Because SeaWorld is dedicated to research and education, the theme park offers certified K–12 teachers in Florida free admission. The SeaWorld Florida Teacher Card is valid for unlimited admission to SeaWorld Orlando through September 2, 2027. All teachers have to do is pre-register on ID.Me with a Department of Education (DOE) number. Plus, Florida Teacher Card holders have the option to add Aquatica Orlando for only $49.99.

If you find yourself visiting the dolphins often, consider investing in an annual pass for the lowest cost per visit. Annual passes often include perks like free guest tickets and discounts on food and merchandise. During the sale, prices for passes are reduced for new members: Save up to 15% on the Bronze Pass, 20% on Silver, 25% on Gold, and 30% on Platinum. Using a SeaWorld Parks promo code annual pass deal can pay for itself in just two visits.

Check if the code is park-specific (for example, a SeaWorld Orlando promo code may not work for San Diego). #6251. JetBlue is Launching a New Domestic First Class—and We Got a First Look

Flying domestic with JetBlue just got an upgrade. On Wednesday, November 11, the airline introduced BlueFirst, a brand-new domestic first class product, ahead of its debut flight on December 8. The cabin is a dedicated section in the first three rows, arranged two-by-two (read: no middle seats). It will be installed across the airline's fleet on planes that do not already have a Mint business class cabin, bringing a domestic first class to the shorter routes for which JetBlue is more commonly known. As Stephanie Evans Greene, the airline’s senior vice president of marketing and brand, tells Condé Nast Traveler, the idea is "premium, but not pretentious."

BlueFirst will begin rolling out across JetBlue’s fleet in early December, beginning with the carrier’s daily Boston–Fort Lauderdale flight and soon followed by its popular Fort Lauderdale–New York LaGuardia route.

The new cabin is a big shift for JetBlue, an airline that for most of its 26 years in business flew economy seats only. The one exception is Mint, a lie-flat business class available on the airline's transcontinental and transatlantic routes, like New York to Los Angeles and London. To be clear: BlueFirst is not a version of Mint, and the two will never appear on the same plane. Mint planes keep Mint, and BlueFirst goes on every other aircraft. Where Mint is a bed, BlueFirst is a recliner, built for the shorter leisure routes that make up most of JetBlue's network.

To test out the BlueFirst product, we checked out the first aircraft with the new cabins installed on the ground at New York—JFK. Here's everything travelers should know before booking.

The first three rows of the plane will be dedicated to BlueFirst, with 12 seats in total.

As for the seat itself, the first thing that will stand out to travelers is just how much more space there is. BlueFirst has only three rows—12 seats total—and each seat is about three inches wider than a standard economy seat, with room to spare in every direction. The seat is spacious enough to hold a passenger and a laptop bag next to them (or a large purse, in my case), and the space in front is just as generous, with up to seven extra inches of legroom compared with JetBlue's regular Main seats. It reclines five inches too, though the recline takes a bit of pressure (hold the button and push back on the seat firmly). Press the button again, and the seat pops right back up. In true JetBlue fashion—this is, after all, the airline that built its name on being the un-stuffy one—there's no curtain cutting the BlueFirst cabin off from the rest of the plane.

Mattress company Tuft & Needle designed the seat cushion using T&N Flex foam.

The seat cushion is made with Tuft & Needle's T&N Flex foam (yes, the mattress company), developed just for JetBlue. It's squishy enough to comfortably sink into, and it responds as you shift, in both the bottom cushion and the backrest. The adjustable headrest also has wings that fold in to cradle your head. "I'll go on record and say I think they're some of the most comfortable recline seats that are out there in domestic first class," Greene says.

BlueFirst passengers receive a blanket and an amenity kit with socks, earbuds, mouthwash, and OSEA Malibu skincare products.

Aside from the bigger, more comfortable seat, BlueFirst gives travelers a slew of other perks. At every seat, there's a 13.3-inch screen with Bluetooth for personal earbuds, USB-A, USB-C, and a regular outlet, plus JetBlue's free Wi-Fi. The overhead bins above the cabin are reserved for BlueFirst passengers, so boarding doesn't come with the usual scramble for space, and each large bifold tray table has a stand for your phone or tablet. Travelers also get a blanket and an amenity kit with socks, earbuds, mouthwash, and OSEA Malibu skincare products, including a lip balm, hand cream, and the fan-favorite calming pulse point oil.

What's more, the perks start before passengers even get on the plane: BlueFirst comes with priority check-in, a faster security lane at more than 30 airports, and Group 1 boarding. Most BlueFirst fares come with two free checked bags—even BlueFirst Base, the cheapest of the three, includes one checked bag.

The dining options in BlueFirst depend on how long your flight is. A bento-inspired box is served on flights of 899 miles or more, with an entrée, a side, and a dessert. The exact menu changes based on the route. Dinner might be a tortellini pasta salad with marinated green olives, a pastrami sandwich with a citrusy cabbage salad, or sesame noodles with crispy wontons and a Szechuan dip. The desserts are a highlight: the pasta comes with a carrot cake with a caramel icing top that's deliciously moist (my personal favorite), and there are colorful macarons and a pistachio chocolate cake on other menus. Breakfast runs from hazelnut-ricotta crêpes to a sweet potato and bean bowl with guacamole and hot sauce, a poached pear, and blueberry chia pudding. There are also kosher, vegan, and gluten-free versions of the boxes.

Drinks in this section of the cabin deserve their own mention, because BlueFirst's come with a twist you won't find on other US airlines. Everything is ordered right from the seatback screen in Mixologist Mode, which lets you build your own cocktail (or mocktail) instead of choosing from a list. You start with a base—a spirit, a soft drink, coffee, a mixer—and add up to four items in total from the full drink menu. The crew then brings the ingredients right to your separate pop-out cocktail tray, and you mix it yourself. There's a limit of two drinks per order, but once the first round lands, you can start the next. The drinks come in real glassware from Fable, on handmade watercolor coasters by New York-based illustrator Danielle Rose Fisher. For anyone not playing bartender, there's also wine from Parcelle, coffee from Cometeer and Joe Coffee, and Smith Teamaker teas.

The new cabin will first roll out on JetBlue flights from Fort Lauderdale to and New York LaGuardia and Boston.

The retrofit should be nearly done by the end of 2027, covering every JetBlue plane that doesn't have Mint.

BlueFirst tickets are currently on sale for travel dates beginning in December. The cabins will be added to more than 30 routes throughout 2026; you'll start seeing the new seats on flights from JFK to Cancún, Liberia, and San Juan beginning in January. However, even on those inaugural routes, not every flight will have BlueFirst right away (it depends on whether a fitted plane is operating that flight). Just over a dozen planes will have the cabin by the end of this year, with the rest of the fleet following through 2027.

By the end of next year, the retrofit should be nearly done, covering every JetBlue plane that doesn't have Mint. Until then, it's worth double-checking before booking since JetBlue notes BlueFirst may only be available on select flights or dates, and planes can be swapped at a moment’s notice depending on equipment needs and maintenance.

Staying at Walt Disney World on hotel points — within walking distance of two theme parks — might sound like a pixie-dust-fueled dream, but it's actually possible if you stay at the Walt Disney World Swan, Dolphin or Swan Reserve.

These large, highly visible properties are actually three adjacent but distinct hotels that share access to amenities.

The Dolphin is the 27-story pyramid that opened in 1990 and is visible from just about every Disney World theme park.

The Swan opened in 1990 and is home to two 47-foot swan statues, while the Swan Reserve is the newest of the trio, having just opened in 2021.

These three resorts are clustered together and are all bookable with Marriott Bonvoy points. This is possible because while they each have Walt Disney World in their names and in their location, the Dolphin is actually a Sheraton, the Swan is a Westin and the Swan Reserve is in Marriott's Autograph Collection.

Related: These are the best credit cards for earning Marriott Bonvoy points

That means that the current welcome bonus with the (see rates and fees) that awards three free night awards (valued up to 50,000 Marriott points each; certain hotels have resort fees) after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first three months of account opening could cover a three-night stay at one of these properties. And that's especially true if you were willing to top up your awards with up to 25,000 additional Marriott points if the nights you wanted cost a few more points than 50,000. Additionally, new cardholders can receive up to $100 in statement credits (up to $50 biannually) after spending $500 on eligible airline purchases (through June 30, 2027).

Generally speaking, the Walt Disney World Dolphin is a large, busy convention hotel with the most on-site restaurants and amenities. The Walt Disney World Swan is comparatively smaller but still a very large, busy hotel that's closest to the Dolphin, with both connected by a covered walkway.

The Swan Reserve is the smallest, most upscale — and most expensive — of the three properties. But combined, these three properties are positively massive with 2,619 rooms, 23 restaurants and lounges, and a host of amenities and facilities.

Due to some wheeling and dealing in the 1980s, the Swan and Dolphin (and later, Swan Reserve) scored some of the best real estate at Walt Disney World.

These resorts are within walking distance of both Epcot and Disney's Hollywood Studios. Or there's a complimentary water taxi that can take you to either of those parks that leaves from the dock between the Dolphin and the Swan.

Only three of Disney's own operated resorts can claim this same feature: Disney's Yacht Club, Disney's Boardwalk and Disney's Beach Club.

All of those are deluxe Disney resorts that regularly start between $600 - $800 per night, where rooms at this trio of properties can start at half that price if you're paying with cash.

Related: How to save hundreds of dollars on a trip to Disney with the Disney Inspire Visa

There are multiple pools at the Swan, Dolphin and Swan Reserve, with each property having at least one pool located directly on-site.

But the most expansive pools are situated closest to the Dolphin, including the grotto pool with waterfalls and a waterslide.

There is also a lap pool in case you want to get a water-based workout in. A great thing about the pools — and other amenities — is that it doesn't matter which of these three hotels you are staying at; you can use all the amenities at the other hotels, too.

But it's not just pools you can pick from; there is a very long list of amenities in case the Disney parks leave you with some downtime.

At the Dolphin, you'll find a good-sized arcade and even a small bowling alley.

Between the Swan and Dolphin, there is also sand volleyball, an outdoor playground area for little kids and even swan-themed paddle boats that guests can take out on the water at no additional cost, as rentals are included in the hefty $50 nightly resort fee.

If you wanted to have a resort day outside the theme parks during your Disney World vacation, the odds are high that there is plenty to do at the Swan, Dolphin and Swan Reserve to keep you entertained.

Each of the three hotels also has its own fitness area for you to still get your workouts in.

If, after all that activity, you want to rest and enjoy a massage or another treatment, there is a Mandara Spa inside the Dolphin.

Believe it or not, the reason you can enjoy these Marriott hotels, located in the heart of Walt Disney World, dates back to disputes and deals in the 1980s.

The hotels have many Disney perks and an on-property Disney location, but they are not actually Disney-owned and operated hotels. And now they are all hotels where you can earn and use Marriott Bonvoy points to stay in the middle of Mickey's kingdom without paying Mickey's exact price tag.

Guests of the Walt Disney World Swan, Dolphin and Swan Reserve get to enjoy some really good Disney benefits that are otherwise mostly reserved only for true on-property Disney World guests.

As mentioned, there are complimentary boats to Epcot and Hollywood Studios from these hotels if you don't want to make the 15-20-minute walk.

There are buses that leave from these hotels to Magic Kingdom or Animal Kingdom. The one downside to the buses vs. those at "true" Disney resorts is that the bus to Magic Kingdom takes you to the Ticket and Transportation Center (TTC) instead of to Magic Kingdom itself. From the TTC, you have to take the monorail or ferry boat to the Magic Kingdom.

If that sounds like a hassle to you, it can be a good time to splurge on a Disney-operated Minnie Van you book in the Lyft app to take you directly to the front of the Magic Kingdom with the money you saved by staying at these hotels instead of actual deluxe Disney resorts.

At these hotels, you will find true Disney gift shops, along with Disney park tickets and Disney vacation planning assistance.

If by which hotel is best you mean the nicest, then the answer is likely the Walt Disney World Swan Reserve. It is not only the newest and most expensive of the three hotels, but also the one that falls under the higher-category Marriott Brand, Autograph Collection.

But everyone has different tastes and priorities for their Disney trip, so each of the three hotels has its own fans.

All three of the Swan, Dolphin and Swan Reserve hotels are great choices for families, but if we have to choose, families with young kids may enjoy the Swan and Dolphin a bit more due to more on-site amenities such as the playground and arcade and a slightly shorter walk to the boats or to Epcot and Hollywood Studios.

There are also more on-site food options at the Dolphin and Swan than you'll find at the Swan Reserve.

In part because of conventions and events that do come to these hotels, no single hotel among the three is always the cheapest. The only real way to know for sure on your dates is to run some searches.

However, the Dolphin is the least expensive of the three on average, whether booking on Marriott points or cash, typically followed by the Swan and then the Swan Reserve.

All the rooms at these hotels are nice, especially once the Dolphin finishes its current renovation, but there are differences among them.

Swan Reserve rooms are likely the nicest between the three, with higher-end finishes, two robes available, walk-in showers, a better coffee maker, etc.

The rooms at the Swan are also nice and have been recently renovated. In my experience, they typically offer one robe, and importantly, two queen beds in the rooms with the two bed option.

The rooms at the Dolphin are currently undergoing renovation to make them more similar in appearance to the Swan. However, a significant difference will remain even after the renovations.

The beds at the Dolphin in rooms with two beds are full-sized or double beds, not queen beds. This makes it a tighter fit if you are putting two people in each bed.

There were no robes in our Dolphin room, and the coffee maker is a step down, which makes sense, as this is a Sheraton rather than the higher-tier brands at the other two hotels.

There are more restaurants at the Swan, Dolphin and Swan Reserve than it makes sense for me to put in a big list here, but I will mention a few of my personal favorite options.

First, I'm a fan of Rosa Mexicano, especially for an easy, fun arrival-night dinner with margaritas — especially if I have a resort credit to put to good use, as I did recently by booking via Amex's Hotel Collection with my .

Amare, a Mediterranean restaurant at the Swan Reserve, and Todd English's bluezoo, a seafood restaurant in the Walt Disney World Dolphin, are two additional standouts for me, though there are plenty of other great picks, too.

And believe it or not, if you order an entrée at Todd English’s bluezoo, Amare, or Il Mulino New York Trattoria, Rosa Mexicano, Bourbon Steak or Kimonos, your kids ages 5 - 12 can get two free hours at the on-site Camp Dolphin. This supervised childcare includes a take-home craft and a snack.

I also enjoy the grab-and-go options that are available at each of these three hotels for an easy muffin and coffee sort of breakfast in the morning.

If you have Marriott Platinum elite status or higher — which you can get just by having the — you can choose free breakfast as your benefit for the stay, which will get you a daily voucher to use in these shops.

I've stayed at these hotels over a dozen times and there is no doubt in my mind that the Swan, Dolphin and Swan Reserve can absolutely be worth it when deciding between them and Disney-owned resorts.

And don't get me wrong — I really love a good, true Disney resort stay with all of the elaborate themes and locations — but the prices for deluxe resorts owned by Disney are often more than the prices that these three resorts charge. At these hotels, you're often paying a price that is more in the Disney moderate, mid-tier resort range (and sometimes even a value range), but getting closer to deluxe-tier location and amenities.

And you can even use some of your hotel credits from certain Amex or Chase cards and book via programs that give you free breakfast, resort credits and more, like I just did via American Express with my to get $450 in bonus savings and inclusions on a recent stay.

So there are ways you can really bring down your total cost here that typically don't work at true Disney resorts, which don't participate in most of those programs, including even using the simple $100 annual Chase Travel hotel credit from the (see rates and fees).

And that's assuming you're even paying cash — you can also use your Marriott points or free night awards here and save your cash for other parts of the trip.

So yes, I absolutely think it is sometimes worth potentially spending less to stay in the middle of it all at the Swan, Dolphin or Swan Reserve and still get the overwhelming majority of the perks of being at a true Disney resort.

There are a lot of great places to stay while on a Walt Disney World vacation, but often you have to make trade-offs. You can have a great location, good value, or an upscale stay, but typically not all three at the same time ... except at the Swan, Dolphin or Swan Reserve, which have the potential to give you the best of all worlds.

While the Swan Reserve is my favorite of the three, I've stayed at all of these hotels multiple times over the years on cash, Marriott points, and even using some of the hotel credits from my various credit cards, and I have every intention of many more stays in the future.

#6249. Great Wolf Lodge Coupons: 50% Off This November

Family vacations come in all shapes and sizes, but sometimes, it’s all about the kids. That’s when places like Great Wolf Lodge come in clutch. Between the indoor water parks, arcades, and arts and crafts, they’re designed for keeping bundles of energy entertained…both kids and kids at heart. I’ve been to a Great Wolf Lodge once (in LaGrange, just outside of Atlanta) and had a ball going down those water slides and playing arcade games, even as a kid-free twenty-something.

The family resort chain has more than 20 properties across North America; most are clustered on the East Coast and in the Midwest, though there are a handful out west too. If a family vacation calls and you’re looking for ways to save on the stay, keep reading.

Great news—Great Wolf Lodge's early Black Friday sale has begun! Book by November 15 for access to room rates starting at $89 for stays taken by February 25, 2027. Browse locations here; the coupon code will be added automatically as you check out. Of note, Great Wolf Lodge Ontario is excluded from this promotion, but many others, including locations in Scottsdale, the Poconos, and the Wisconsin Dells, are taking part.

While last-minute discounts do exist, it also pays to plan ahead. Save up to 50% when you book your stay at least 60 days in advance with the Great Wolf Lodge promo code ESAVER. This coupon applies to a range of suite styles, from standard Family Suites to larger themed Wolf Den or KidCabin suites. The longer you stay, the more you’ll save—and Great Wolf recently upped the ante with 30% off one-night stays, 40% off two-night stays, and 50% for three-plus night stays. This offer is ideal for guests looking for a Great Wolf Lodge promo code while planning for fall or winter vacations. Of notes, this offer may not be valid during holiday and blackout periods, and cannot be combined with any other discount or promotional offers.

For more short-term plans, use Great Wolf Lodge’s discount code TRIPLEFUN to take up to 40% off your total stay when staying three nights or longer within 60 days of booking. The length of stay requirements for this Great Wolf Lodge coupon mean you’ll have more time to fully experience all of the lodge activities, from the water park to the ropes course and arcade. Of note, Great Wolf Lodge Niagara is excluded from the deal.

If you’re planning a weekend trip (or a shorter mid-week trip!), use promo code MOREFUN to save 30% on two-night bookings for stays within 60 days of purchase. Again, this code is good for the rest of the year, so keep it tucked in the back of your mind if you’ve got a later-in-the-year trip brewing.

Special discounted rates on Great Wolf Lodge day passes are available for military members (active, retired, and veteran), teachers, fire and emergency medical service personnel, medical providers, nurses, 911 dispatchers, police, government employees, and correctional officers looking for a respite. If you work in one of these professions, use the Great Wolf Lodge discount code WPHEROES to access reduced pricing on stays. This code is good through the end of 2028, and you’ll need to verify your status using ID.me.

Grandparents and older parents can get in on the fun with exclusive savings for guests aged 65 and older when using the promo code SENIORS. Proof of age is required at check-in to validate this Great Wolf Lodge discount code. More good news: It’s often combinable with other lodge perks to maximize savings when traveling with the whole family. Great Wolf Lodge Niagara is excluded from this deal.

Members of AAA, AARP, or other vehicle clubs can also save on lodge bookings. Enter your membership details to activate the Great Wolf Lodge AAA discount or Great Wolf Lodge AARP discount. Plan to bring your card with you, as membership cards must also be presented upon arrival. Right now, there is a promo code DRIVER that takes up to 30% off your bill.

One other reliable way to save: Join the Voyagers Club for free to earn points and exclusive members-only deals. Members get early access to Great Wolf Lodge promotion code releases and seasonal sales. They’ll also earn Voyagers Points for money spent at the lodge, which can be redeemed for future stays or on-site amenities.

You'll get a point for every $10 spent on bookings, package add-ons, cabanas, ancillary purchases like late checkout, and on-site spending charged to the suite, including food and retail. Points are not earned on any alcohol purchases, taxes, gratuities, fees, or on-site purchases not charged to the suite. You can check your points balance at any time in your Great Wolf profile, and redeem them by booking directly on greatwolf.com while logged into your account.

Having trouble with a promo code? There are a few things you can do to fix that. First, double check that the code is spelled correctly, with no extra spaces or typos. If all looks good, check the details of the promo code to ensure it's still active and hasn't expired. Some discount codes exclude certain locations, so make sure your booking meets any necessary criteria to qualify. If everything looks good and your Great Wolf Lodge promo code still isn't working, clear your browser's cache and give the page a refresh. When in doubt, contact the brand's customer service team for help (which varies by location).
